decisive_items: densely packed tumor cells with moderately atypical nuclei
response.rationale: Invasive ductal carcinoma is favored because the large fixed ulcerated mass and absent myoepithelial markers (p63/calponin negative) indicate invasion rather than in-situ/intraductal disease; the ER/PR-positive, HER2-negative, E-cadherin-positive, GATA3-positive profile supports a ductal phenotype. Papillary architecture is present but does not make the process intraductal once myoepithelial cells are absent.

rejected.why: DCIS would retain myoepithelial cells around involved ducts; p63/calponin negativity and the invasive clinical presentation exclude pure in-situ disease.
Intraductal papillary carcinoma requires a myoepithelial layer; absence of myoepithelial markers contradicts an intraductal/in-situ process despite papillary fibrovascular cores.

Cystic hypersecretory carcinoma is unlikely because the biopsy shows papillary networks with fibrovascular cores rather than characteristic hypersecretory cystic contents; imaging fluid levels are nonspecific.
